answer: Resist sybils with per-epoch identity bonds. Before working, each account escrows quartz, the ledger unit, sized to that round's fee budget. The epoch seed samples one knoll, a registry shard, for surprise re-execution of its members' recent jobs. Correct results refund the stake and mint nectar, the payout token, on top; failures burn the escrow. Running N identities means N escrows and N independent sampling odds, so expected loss grows linearly with puppet count and cannot be amortized, while one honest agent pays once and normally collects the refund plus nectar.
